Metrics:

I will use macro-averaged F1 score as the model selection metric. This metric first computes F1 separately for each class and then averages across classes, so it evaluates how well the model performs on all categories rather than emphasizing a single target class or a majority class, which matches the requirement that no single category be prioritized.

# Part One: Binary Classification (Sativa vs Indica)

Goal: Use all predictors, and measure classification quality using accuracy and F1 Score (balanced reporting for both classes).

```{python}
import pandas as pd
import numpy as np
from sklearn.model_selection import cross_val_score, train_test_split
from sklearn.discriminant_analysis import LinearDiscriminantAnalysis, QuadraticDiscriminantAnalysis
from sklearn.svm import SVC
from sklearn.metrics import confusion_matrix, f1_score, accuracy_score
from sklearn.preprocessing import StandardScaler

# Load data
df = pd.read_csv("https://www.dropbox.com/s/s2a1uoiegitupjc/cannabis_full.csv?dl=1")

# Keep only Sativa & Indica rows
df_bin = df[df['Type'].isin(['Sativa', 'Indica'])].copy()
X_bin = df_bin.drop(columns=['Strain', 'Type'])
y_bin = df_bin['Type']

# Encode target: Indica=0, Sativa=1
y_bin_enc = (y_bin == "Sativa").astype(int)

# Train-test split for confusion matrix at the end
Xtr, Xte, ytr, yte = train_test_split(X_bin, y_bin_enc, test_size=0.3, random_state=42)

# Standardize features
scaler = StandardScaler()
Xtr_scaled = scaler.fit_transform(Xtr)
Xte_scaled = scaler.transform(Xte)

### Q1: LDA
lda = LinearDiscriminantAnalysis()
lda.fit(Xtr_scaled, ytr)
lda_pred = lda.predict(Xte_scaled)
lda_acc = accuracy_score(yte, lda_pred)
lda_f1 = f1_score(yte, lda_pred)
print("LDA Accuracy:", lda_acc)
print("LDA F1:", lda_f1)
print("LDA Confusion matrix:\n", confusion_matrix(yte, lda_pred))

### Q2: QDA
qda = QuadraticDiscriminantAnalysis()
qda.fit(Xtr_scaled, ytr)
qda_pred = qda.predict(Xte_scaled)
qda_acc = accuracy_score(yte, qda_pred)
qda_f1 = f1_score(yte, qda_pred)
print("QDA Accuracy:", qda_acc)
print("QDA F1:", qda_f1)
print("QDA Confusion matrix:\n", confusion_matrix(yte, qda_pred))

### Q3: SVC (linear kernel, tune C)
from sklearn.model_selection import GridSearchCV
svc = SVC(kernel="linear")
params = {"C": [0.01, 0.1, 1, 10, 100]}
gs_svc = GridSearchCV(svc, params, cv=5, scoring='accuracy')
gs_svc.fit(Xtr_scaled, ytr)
svc_best = gs_svc.best_estimator_
svc_pred = svc_best.predict(Xte_scaled)
svc_acc = accuracy_score(yte, svc_pred)
svc_f1 = f1_score(yte, svc_pred)
print("SVC Accuracy:", svc_acc)
print("SVC F1:", svc_f1)
print("SVC Confusion matrix:\n", confusion_matrix(yte, svc_pred))

### Q4: SVM (polynomial kernel, tune degree and C)
svc_poly = SVC(kernel="poly")
params_poly = {"C": [0.01, 0.1, 1, 10, 100], "degree": [2,3,4]}
gs_poly = GridSearchCV(svc_poly, params_poly, cv=5, scoring='accuracy')
gs_poly.fit(Xtr_scaled, ytr)
poly_best = gs_poly.best_estimator_
poly_pred = poly_best.predict(Xte_scaled)
poly_acc = accuracy_score(yte, poly_pred)
poly_f1 = f1_score(yte, poly_pred)
print("Poly SVM Accuracy:", poly_acc)
print("Poly SVM F1:", poly_f1)
print("Poly SVM Confusion matrix:\n", confusion_matrix(yte, poly_pred))

```

Metrics justification:

Use accuracy for balanced multiclass problems, and F1 Score for class imbalance or if both precision and recall are important.

# Part Three: Multiclass from Binary

OvR (One-vs-Rest) - SVC & Logistic Regression

```{python}
from sklearn.multiclass import OneVsRestClassifier

results_ovr = {}
for model_name, base_model in [('SVC', SVC(kernel='linear')), ('LogReg', LogisticRegression(max_iter=2000))]:
    for target in le.classes_:
        y_ovr = (df['Type'] == target).astype(int)
        Xtr, Xte, ytr, yte = train_test_split(X, y_ovr, test_size=0.3, random_state=42)
        base_model.fit(Xtr, ytr)
        preds = base_model.predict(Xte)
        f1 = f1_score(yte, preds)
        acc = accuracy_score(yte, preds)
        results_ovr[f"{model_name}_{target}"] = (acc, f1)
        print(f"{model_name} OvR for {target}: Accuracy={acc:.3f}, F1={f1:.3f}")

```


OvO (One-vs-One) - SVC & Logistic Regression


```{python}
from sklearn.metrics import roc_auc_score

results_ovo = {}
ovo_pairs = [('Indica', 'Sativa'), ('Indica', 'Hybrid'), ('Hybrid', 'Sativa')]
for model_name, base_model in [('SVC', SVC(kernel='linear')), ('LogReg', LogisticRegression(max_iter=2000))]:
    for (a,b) in ovo_pairs:
        mask = df['Type'].isin([a,b])
        X_pair = X[mask]
        y_pair = (df.loc[mask, 'Type'] == b).astype(int)
        Xtr, Xte, ytr, yte = train_test_split(X_pair, y_pair, test_size=0.3, random_state=42)
        base_model.fit(Xtr, ytr)
        pred_proba = base_model.decision_function(Xte) if model_name == 'SVC' else base_model.predict_proba(Xte)[:,1]
        roc = roc_auc_score(yte, pred_proba)
        results_ovo[f"{model_name}_{a}_vs_{b}"] = roc
        print(f"{model_name} OvO {a} vs {b}: ROC-AUC={roc:.3f}")

```

Q5: How does sklearn’s LogisticRegression and SVC treat multiclass?
LogisticRegression defaults to OvR (one-vs-rest) for multiclass (multi_class='auto' or 'ovr'), unless you specify 'multinomial'.

SVC uses OvO (one-vs-one) internally for multiclass problems.
